name: NVIDIA shader caches
summary: Compiled graphics shaders the NVIDIA driver keeps for your games.
advice: Suggested when a game crashes on launch, stutters, flickers or shows visual glitches, or after a big driver change. Not needed after every driver update.
facts: The driver rebuilds these files the next time a game runs
The first launch after cleaning can be a little slower while shaders rebuild
Drivers version their caches, so old shaders are ignored on their own
A few index files are held by the driver and are removed at the next restart
benefit: Frees disk space and can clear crashes or stutter caused by a damaged cache.
risk: None. Only regenerable cache files are removed.

name: AMD shader caches
summary: Compiled graphics shaders the AMD driver keeps for your games.
advice: Suggested when a game crashes, stutters or shows glitches. Not needed after every driver update.
facts: The driver rebuilds these files the next time a game runs
The first launch after cleaning can be a little slower
Covers the DirectX 9, DirectX, DXC, OpenGL and Vulkan caches
benefit: Frees disk space and can clear problems caused by a damaged cache.
risk: None. Only regenerable cache files are removed.

name: Intel shader cache
summary: Compiled graphics shaders the Intel driver keeps.
advice: Suggested when a game crashes, stutters or shows glitches on Intel graphics.
facts: The driver rebuilds these files when a game runs
The first launch after cleaning can be a little slower
benefit: Frees disk space and can clear problems caused by a damaged cache.
risk: None. Only regenerable cache files are removed.

name: Windows DirectX shader cache
summary: The shader cache Windows keeps for every DirectX game.
advice: Suggested when a DirectX game crashes or glitches. Windows rebuilds it by itself.
facts: Windows ships a Disk Cleanup entry for this cache
The cache is tied to the driver version, so old entries are ignored
The first launch after cleaning can be a little slower
benefit: Frees disk space and can clear problems caused by a damaged cache.
risk: None. Only regenerable cache files are removed.

name: Steam shader caches
summary: Shaders Steam pre-builds for your games, kept in every Steam library.
advice: Suggested when a Steam game crashes or stutters, or to win back disk space. Steam rebuilds them.
facts: Found in the steamapps folder of every Steam library
Steam can download or rebuild them when you start a game
Games and saves are never touched
benefit: Frees disk space, often several gigabytes.
risk: None. Games stay installed.

name: Discord cache
summary: Images and web files Discord keeps for faster loading.
advice: Suggested when Discord is slow, shows broken images or uses a lot of space. Close Discord first.
facts: Your login and settings are kept
Discord rebuilds the cache as you use it
Covers Discord, PTB and Canary
benefit: Frees disk space and fixes a stuck or damaged cache.
risk: None.

name: Epic Games Launcher web cache
summary: Pages and images the Epic launcher keeps.
advice: Suggested when the Epic Games Launcher shows blank pages or loads slowly. Close it first.
facts: Your login and installed games are kept
The launcher rebuilds the cache when it starts
benefit: Fixes a stuck store page and frees space.
risk: None.

name: Battle.net cache
summary: Files the Battle.net app keeps for faster loading.
advice: Suggested when the Battle.net app is slow or shows blank pages. Close it first.
facts: Your login and installed games are kept
Battle.net rebuilds the cache when it starts
benefit: Fixes a stuck app and frees space.
risk: None.

name: Steam web browser cache
summary: The cache behind the Steam store and library pages.
advice: Suggested when Steam pages are blank or slow. This is what Steam's own Delete web browser cache button clears.
facts: Your login and games are kept
Steam rebuilds the cache when it starts
benefit: Fixes blank Steam pages and frees space.
risk: None.

name: EA app cache
summary: Files the EA app keeps for faster loading.
advice: Suggested when the EA app is slow or stuck. Close it first.
facts: Your login and games are kept
The app rebuilds the cache when it starts
benefit: Fixes a stuck app and frees space.
risk: None.

name: Ubisoft Connect cache
summary: Files Ubisoft Connect keeps for faster loading.
advice: Suggested when Ubisoft Connect is slow or stuck. Close it first.
facts: Your login and games are kept
The app rebuilds the cache when it starts
benefit: Fixes a stuck app and frees space.
risk: None.

name: GOG Galaxy web cache
summary: Pages and images GOG Galaxy keeps.
advice: Suggested when GOG Galaxy shows blank pages or loads slowly. Close it first.
facts: Your login and games are kept
Galaxy rebuilds the cache when it starts
benefit: Fixes a stuck app and frees space.
risk: None.

name: World of Warcraft cache
summary: The Cache folder of each installed World of Warcraft version.
advice: Suggested after a patch if the game shows wrong items or stale data. Close the game first.
facts: Only the Cache folder is touched
The WTF, Interface and Data folders, your settings and add-ons are never touched
The game rebuilds the cache on the next launch
benefit: Clears stale data after patches and frees space.
risk: None. The first launch loads a little slower.

name: Temporary files
summary: Files programs left in the user and system temp folders.
advice: Suggested for everyone. Only files untouched for a day are removed, so a running installer is safe.
facts: Only files older than 24 hours are removed
Files in use are left alone
Covers your temp folder and the Windows temp folder
benefit: Frees disk space.
risk: None.

name: Thumbnail cache
summary: The picture previews File Explorer keeps for your folders.
advice: Suggested if thumbnails look wrong or stale. Windows rebuilds them as you browse.
facts: Only the thumbcache database files are removed
Some files are in use by Explorer and are left alone
Windows rebuilds thumbnails when you open folders
benefit: Fixes wrong or missing previews and frees space.
risk: None. Folders with many pictures load previews slower once.

name: Delivery Optimization files
summary: Update files Windows kept to share with other PCs.
advice: Suggested for everyone. Disk Cleanup lists these too.
facts: Windows downloads them again only if it needs them
Files in use are left alone
benefit: Frees disk space, often a few gigabytes.
risk: None.

name: Windows Update downloads
summary: Update files already downloaded to the SoftwareDistribution folder.
advice: Suggested only when no update is installing. Skip it while Windows Update is working.
facts: Windows downloads them again if it needs them
No service is stopped, so files in use are left alone
Does not remove installed updates
benefit: Frees disk space and can fix a stuck update download.
risk: Low. An update in progress may have to download again.

name: Prefetch
summary: Startup hints Windows keeps for apps.
advice: Optional and rarely useful. Clearing it does not make games or Windows faster.
facts: Windows rebuilds the hints as you launch apps
Does not make anything faster
Apps may start slightly slower once
benefit: Frees a little space.
risk: None.

name: Error reports and crash dumps
summary: Reports and dumps Windows saved after app crashes.
advice: Suggested only if you are not chasing a crash. These files are the evidence when something keeps failing.
facts: Windows does not recreate old reports
Includes your crash dumps and the Windows error report archive
Keep them if a developer or support asked for them
benefit: Frees disk space.
risk: Low. You lose the evidence of past crashes.

name: GPU crash dumps
summary: Dumps Windows saves when the graphics driver stops responding.
advice: Suggested to win back space. Keep them if a graphics driver maker may ask for one.
facts: One dump from a graphics timeout can be several gigabytes
They are safe to delete
Windows saves a new one if the driver fails again
benefit: Frees disk space, sometimes many gigabytes.
risk: Low. You lose the evidence of past graphics crashes.

name: Recycle Bin
summary: Empty the Recycle Bin on every drive.
advice: Suggested only after you checked that nothing in it is needed. This cannot be undone.
facts: Emptied through Windows, so it is the same as the Empty Recycle Bin button
Files cannot be recovered afterward
Covers every drive
benefit: Frees disk space.
risk: Medium. Deleted files cannot be restored.

name: Event Viewer logs
summary: Save a copy of the classic Windows event logs, then clear them. Not the Security log.
advice: Not suggested for most people. The logs are capped in size, so this frees little, and the history is what explains crashes and failures. Use it only to start a clean log while you test something.
facts: Each log is saved as an .evtx file in the Clarion data folder first. A log that cannot be saved is not cleared
Open a saved file in Event Viewer to read the old events
The Security log is never cleared
Windows records that a log was cleared
The saved copies take about as much space as the logs, so nothing is freed until you delete them
benefit: A clean log to watch while you test something.
risk: Medium. The old events leave Event Viewer. They stay readable in the saved copies only.

name: Driver installer leftovers
summary: Folders the AMD and NVIDIA installers unpack on the system drive.
advice: Suggested only if you will not roll the driver back. They are the files used to reinstall it.
facts: Covers C:\AMD and C:\NVIDIA\DisplayDriver
Your installed driver is not affected
Remove them only if you do not need to roll back
benefit: Frees disk space, often a few gigabytes.
risk: Low. You need to download the driver again to reinstall it.
